title: Pilot Accelerator: Inference Playbook (mini-deck, sprint draft)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, skimmable mini-playbook for SDRs/AE+platform-engineer pairs to scope and run a 2-week inference pilot. Focus: demonstrate measurable latency/cost wins with Redwood routing + caching in a real app flow. Not a full training deck — this is a field-ready checklist + slide script for short customer meetings.

Audience:
- Primary: Platform/Integration engineers + Engineering managers evaluating inference economics
- Secondary: Product managers and solution architects who care about latency, availability, and cost per 1k requests

High-level slide map (7 slides, ~10 minutes):
1) One-liner opener (30s)
   - Slide title: "Pilot Accelerator: Prove inference economics in 2 weeks"
   - Speaker note: quick positioning — hosted API for fast proof-of-value, dedicated/private for scale. Call out measurable KPIs we can change: p95 latency, tokens/sec cost, tail error rate.

2) Why this pilot (45s)
   - Bullet: reduce token cost by 20–50% for high-throughput flows with smart batching + prefix caching
   - Bullet: safeguard latency with region routing + lightweight fallbacks for model variants
   - Note: use a real customer path (e.g., autocomplete, chat search, summarization pipeline) not synthetic benchmark.

3) What we deliver (1 min)
   - Live baseline: instrumented measurement of current calls (p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens)
   - 2-week configuration: routing policy + caching + mini quantization plan (if private/dedicated)
   - Result deliverable: short report + runbook + A/B comparison metrics + a short recorded demo

4) Quick technical checklist (2–3 min) — field checklist for eng partner:
   - Integration points: identify endpoint(s) and request patterns (avg seq len, burstiness, concurrency)
   - Byte/sample collection: provide 200–500 representative requests and example prompts
   - Required access: API key for a test workspace, optional VPC peering for private pilot
   - Minimal telemetry to add (if absent): request_id, route_tag, model_version, token_count, latency_ms
   - Fallback plan: pre-approve compatible model variant list and a routing fallback policy (in case of capacity/latency issues)

5) Sales-facing battlecard snippets (1–2 min) — rapid responses to common objections:
   - "We can't risk regressions": we run prompt-preserving canary (A/B on 5–10 eval prompts) + quality acceptance gates; rollback automated
   - "Latency will spike with batching": continuous batching adapts by SLO band — we set hard latency cutoff and route to lower-batch-fast-paths if needed
   - "We must keep data on-prem": private pilot option with local inference; we can mirror routing policies and metrics to the console
   - "Pricing surprise": transparent pilot billing estimate included in scope; we show pre/post cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly impact

6) Example scripts and templates (1–2 min)
   - Email opener to eng partner: short template with required artifacts (endpoint, sample traffic, desired KPI)
   - Slack DM to solutions engineer: checklist + runbook stub link
   - Quick CLI to capture baseline: tiny curl + jq snippet to extract timing and token-count headers (included as appendix)

7) Success criteria and next steps (30–45s)
   - Success metrics: p95 latency reduction >= 15% OR cost per 1k tokens reduction >= 20% while preserving evaluation pass rate >= 95% on provided prompts
   - Milestones: day 0 instrument & baseline; day 3 config + small canary; day 7 expand traffic; day 14 report & decision (go/no-go/scale)

Appendix / Field notes (freeform, notes-to-self style):
- Pilot sizing heuristics: for interactive chat flows aim to batch window <= 50ms; for high-throughput embedding flows prioritize micro-batching with caching of static prefixes
- Typical ramp constraints: customers often forget to provide representative long-tail prompts (be explicit: give 10% of examples with >512 tokens)
- Security checklist: if customer requests KMS/HSM integration for Private, log ticket with infra-privates team (ref: JIRA-RDW-1892)
- Quick ROI calc example (for AE to use in follow-up):
   Baseline: 10M tokens/month @ $0.008/1k = $80/month
   Post-optim: 10M tokens/month effective @ $0.005/1k = $50/month => $30/month saving (37% reduction).
   Show how dedicated reserved capacity changes math — include commit-level discounts in appendix.

Open questions we need to decide before next sprint:
- Do we pre-create a sample dedicated pool for pilots or spin per-customer? (ops cost tradeoff)
- Standardize a 10-prompt eval harness for quality gate? (product + applied-ml alignment)

Action items (owners):
- Maya: finalize slide visuals + sample curl snippets (due 2026-03-15)
- Liam: confirm pilot pool options with infra (due 2026-03-11) — pending
- Elena: update AE playbook page with ROI calc template (Confluence link above)

Speaker notes / quick talking points for AE:
- "We'll treat your traffic like a real endpoint — measure first, then apply small changes that preserve behavior and cut cost/latency."
- "The pilot is low-commit and designed to produce a clear decision at the end: scale, adjust, or stop."
- "We bring both the runtime tuning and the rollout policy; we don't ask you to rebuild your app."

Appendix: sample curl (to paste on a single slide)
- curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rwd-neo-small","input":"<sample>"}' 
  | jq '. | {id: .request_id, tokens: .usage.total_tokens, latency: .meta.timeline.total_ms}'

Notes to self: keep language crisp, avoid deep infra detail on first customer call. This doc should live alongside a runnable repo of sample scripts (linked above).
